# The Xcode project stays generated by XcodeGen, pinned

*Decided September 2026 (issue #165).* Since Xcode 16, buildable folders give a committed project whose target follows a folder, so XcodeGen was weighed against retiring it. It stays. `project.yml` is the most reviewable form of the project, and the one an agent can edit safely: most changes here come from agents, and editing `project.pbxproj` by hand is not safe, while synchronized folders do nothing for settings, capabilities or a new target. A committed project also picks up noise from every Xcode upgrade (`objectVersion`, `LastUpgradeCheck`), which generation absorbs.

What it cost was an unpinned install: CI ran `brew install xcodegen` and took whatever version Homebrew had. The Makefile now names the release and its zip's SHA-256 (`XCODEGEN_VERSION`, `XCODEGEN_SHA256`), `make xcodegen-install` downloads exactly that and checks it into `.build/xcodegen`, `make xcodeproj` runs that copy when there is one, and CI installs through that target. Contributors can keep Homebrew's: `make xcodeproj` warns when the installed version is another, rather than failing, since the project is generated and gitignored.

`ENABLE_PREVIEWS` is off until the first `#Preview` exists. `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` stays committed: it is only the maintainer's team ID, it is what lets `make run` sign out of the box, and everyone else builds with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, as CI does.
